critical_path.rationale: Longest-path computation is BLOCKED pending cycle resolution — a longest path is undefined on a graph containing a cycle (the walk would never terminate). This is NOT the same as 'no critical path exists'; it is a hard precondition failure. Escalating cycle_check.status: FAIL to a human rather than silently dropping one of the three depends-on edges (policy-engine -> claim-submission-service, claim-submission-service -> approver-dashboard-service, or approver-dashboard-service -> policy-engine) to make the graph acyclic — each edge is individually plausible per impact-assessment.md's own stated rationale, and only a human with authority over the policy-engine/dashboard/submission teams' actual build order can decide which dependency is wrong, not this agent.

content.execution_summary:
• Produced 4 nodes (3 components, 1 external dependency) and 5 edges.
• cycle_check: FAIL — DFS traversal starting from policy-engine reached claim-submission-service, then approver-dashboard-service, then found policy-engine already on the recursion stack: a genuine back-edge, confirming the cycle policy-engine -> claim-submission-service -> approver-dashboard-service -> policy-engine.
• critical_path: NOT computed — undefined while a cycle exists; nodes left empty rather than guessed at.
• Key decision: did NOT drop any of the 3 depends-on edges to force acyclicity. Each is individually grounded in impact-assessment.md's own stated rationale (policy validation, display ordering, threshold calibration) — resolving the contradiction between them requires a human decision about actual build sequencing, not an automated guess.
• Knowledge bases consulted: kb-L1-enterprise-architecture — confirmed none of the 3 disputed dependencies is resolved by an existing architecture pattern.
• Guardrails evaluated: gr-L1-output-schema-validator (FAIL — cyclic graph correctly rejected from validating as a normal success; this is the guardrail firing as designed, not a defect), gr-L1-pii-detection (pass), gr-L1-hallucination-check (pass — no edge invented, all 3 came from impact-assessment.md verbatim), gr-L1-consistency-check (FAIL — the 3 dependency statements are mutually inconsistent when combined, which is exactly what triggered this escalation).
• Gaps flagged: escalate to HITL — ask the impact assessor / product-and-architecture owners which one of the 3 depends-on statements is actually wrong (or whether policy-engine calibration should be decoupled from real-time dashboard history, e.g. via a periodic batch job instead of a live dependency) before this graph can be finalised.
